expectations.text: Every reported finding gives concrete evidence (a count, measurement, named consumer/caller, or failing input) rather than only restating a rule.

suggestions.assertion: The review flags comparing forest[index].kind against the string "call_expression" inside the per-node loop in CollectCalls.
suggestions.reason: Ambiguous about why the comparison is a defect. SnapshotNode.kind is declared `kind: string` (source_snapshot/Snapshot.chibi), and the package's own `Is` helper (package_compiler/Tree.chibi:51) does the same `forest[node].kind == kind` comparison. with_skill noticed the per-node string comparison and declined it with accurate reasoning. without_skill flagged the line only to say 'use Is()', which keeps the same string comparison. A lenient grader would pass without_skill for a style point and fail with_skill for a deliberate, correct decline. Reword it to name the expected point, for example 'flags the per-node string comparison as cost and proposes an interned or enum kind', or drop it if declining because the forest stores kinds as strings is acceptable.

suggestions.assertion: The review does not recommend splitting any function purely because of its length.
suggestions.reason: Nearly always passes on this diff. No function in the commit is longer than about 20 lines, so neither review was tempted to split one. A11 (defensive checks) is also weak. To make these discriminate, seed a long but cohesive function, or a spot where a defensive check looks attractive.

Only one assertion separates the runs. 10 of 12 have the same result for both runs (A1-3 and A5-12 pass for both, A4 fails for both), and only A10 (concrete evidence) differs. The baseline review finds every seeded defect.

No assertion covers the most severe true defects, and both reviews found them. (a) CallCensus.chibi isn't listed in asset_compiler/CompilerSources.txt: it lists 18 package_compiler files and the folder has 19. compiler_bootstrap.c packages_complete therefore rejects the package with 'is in the package of a compiler source but ... does not list it', which breaks compiler load and recovery. (b) `strings.Concat` doesn't exist; only `Concatenate(a: string[])` at Strings.chibi:551. (c) CalleeName passes `end` where `strings.Slice(value, start, count)` takes a count, so every callee text is wrong. (d) CollectCalls iterates the whole multi-document forest but reads offsets from one document's text. (e) `counts` keys carry a 'call:' prefix that the sites don't have, and MarkDead never updates `counts`. (f) For packed arrays, pin_array_count_type's answer is always count or 0. Found only by without_skill: element `type_name` is set inconsistently for scalars (src/execution/intrinsics.c:580 sets "int"; :2453, :2467, :2545 and :2563 leave it NULL), so `type_name` is an unreliable discriminator. Whether these were seeded or accidental, add assertions for at least (a) and (c).

eval_feedback.overall: The seeded defects are too easy: the baseline catches all of them. Only A10 separates the runs. The highest-severity bugs in the commit (unlisted compiler source, missing strings.Concat, Slice count/end mixup, cross-document offsets) have no assertion, and A4 needs a clearer statement of the expected point.
